scope: P2 owner-only moderation status. Not complete account security, P0-P11, installed Windows or release acceptance.
implemented: GET /api/users/me/account-status reads the authenticated owner's fresh platform-ban flag and active server bans/timeouts. No arbitrary user-ID selector, trust score, pending-report claim, moderator identity, private moderation notes or invented healthy badge is added.

One SQL statement provides an internally consistent snapshot. Expired restrictions are filtered using the existing enforcement timestamp contract. Removed membership does not hide an active ban from its target.

Reason, server name, applied/expiry times and permanent state are shown. Results paginate at 50 with one-row lookahead and deterministic ordering. Refresh replaces the list; more results append without duplicate identities.

Owner affinity is mandatory; bots are refused; sensitive responses use no-store. Database and network errors never manufacture an empty or healthy snapshot. Previously loaded data is explicitly described as potentially stale on failure.
TR/EN security subsection, retry, loading, real last-check timestamp and account-generation/request-revision guards. Moderation text is rendered as text rather than HTML.
Security subsection heading IDs now agree with workspace-generated IDs, preserving MFA/session/account-status region names after the heading collector runs.

automated_checks.note: Actual SQLite owner isolation, no-member ban visibility, permanent and expiring records, fresh platform ban/unban, unknown-owner rejection, 50+1 pagination and invalid offsets.
Unauthenticated/nil users, bots, missing/mismatched owner, invalid offset, ignored foreign user query, database failure and no-store; route golden updated.

Initial failure never displays a healthy result, retry, real text/escaping, page append and replaced-login response guard. The later refresh label and matching heading ID were included in the final regression run.
Full packages passed after account-status integration, atomic credential writes and migration 093 regression tests. Optional external-service acceptance is not implied.
After final heading IDs, labels and all implementation edits. Existing act/navigation and intentional failure-probe console messages remain.
Web TypeScript/production build only. Existing config-loader, dependency eval and chunk/import warnings remain.

local_runtime.environment: Reused own Ego task space 10, browser 3131 and isolated API 9191. Only preexisting throwaway acceptance accounts and newly generated test servers were used; no screenshot personal accounts or production data was imported.
observations: A separate local owner created a server/invite; the target fixture joined. A real API communication timeout appeared with its actual reason and end time in the target browser.
The owner then applied a real expiring ban. Refresh displayed both restriction rows and their real source data. This also demonstrated that membership removal does not hide the ban.

Owner unban and timeout removal followed by browser refresh produced the genuine empty state. Only the two new identified acceptance servers were removed; independent fixture login sessions were ended.

At 1440x900 and 390x844 the actual restriction rows were readable; mobile document width was 390. The browser confirmed every security section aria-labelledby resolved to an existing heading. Both screenshots were visually inspected.
execution_notes: An initial browser wait used a pre-collector heading ID and timed out. Inspection revealed the workspace assigns canonical IDs; component region IDs were aligned with those canonical IDs.

Joining a new fixture server through a second protocol client closed the browser settings workspace. The first attempt's own new server was removed in cleanup. A subsequent fresh fixture was created and settings were explicitly reopened after joining; actions were not blindly replayed on the old server.
The first lint run identified synchronous state setting through the initial effect. Initial fetching was separated from manual refresh state changes; later lint completed successfully.

remaining_acceptance: Installed Windows UI, remote libSQL, remaining 768/1024/2560 viewports, 200 percent zoom, real screen-reader reading and overall visual-reference acceptance.

Live platform-ban notifications, recovery/appeal UX and account lifecycle. Existing platform-ban enforcement still denies login and authenticated APIs; this owner endpoint intentionally does not bypass that enforcement.

Reports are not penalties, and no strikes/history are synthesized from report counts. This view is limited explicitly to current platform status and the existing server ban/timeout enforcement records.
Overall implementation and release acceptance remain open. No commit/push/merge, production deployment or Windows update has been performed.
